sections.h2: Ways to sell a Southlake house
sections.html:
Owners in Southlake choose among an agent, a private sale and a cash bid. What you hope to get, what shape the house is in and when you must close drive the decision. The city sits at State Highway 114 and Farm Road 1709, seventeen miles north of Fort Worth, next to Grapevine, Keller and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. Most houses here went up within the last four decades, so buyers will think hard about how old your HVAC, roof and finishes are.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, with staging, showings and a lender's timeline to endure.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and take on the marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash bid: a quick as-is sale, priced to cover the buyer's repair costs and risk.

Compare offers by the check you would actually receive once the loan, taxes and closing costs are paid. The headline price can mislead.

Southlake sits across the line between Tarrant and Denton counties. Its tax page links to both the Tarrant County Appraisal District and the Denton County Appraisal District, and the side your house sits on decides its appraisal district, tax collector and county clerk.

Your tax bill and your deed both name the county, and the bill also lists the taxing units. Read them before anyone orders a payoff or records a deed, then give copies to the title company at the outset so it contacts the right office and clerk.

sections.h2: Why the county line matters at closing
sections.html: A Denton County parcel and a Tarrant County parcel can sit a few blocks apart yet use different offices for almost every step. The appraisal district, the tax office quoting your payoff and the clerk who records your deed all follow the county. A seller who calls the wrong one loses days. Write the county at the top of your checklist, and tell each buyer which one applies so their title company starts in the right place. Southlake's proximity to Keller, Grapevine and the airport draws buyers from several directions, and many will not know the split exists.

sections.h2: The city homestead exemption and tax pages
sections.html: Southlake offers a 20 percent homestead exemption and describes it as the highest state law allows. Texas now requires every city to post a notice pointing to the appraisal district database where a parcel's estimated tax appears. Southlake complies with links to the Tarrant and Denton districts. The city also offers a form for property tax and budget questions. Search for your own parcel in the correct district's database instead of trusting a neighborhood average.

The statewide schedule shapes what a seller owes at closing. Values and homestead status freeze on January 1, and the tax lien attaches the same day.

Dates a Southlake seller should know
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set, exemptions are decided and the tax lien attaches
April 1Homestead owners receive notices of appraised value
May 15Usual protest deadline, or 30 days after the notice if that is later
October 1Bills go out
November 30First half is due if you split the payment
January 31Normal due date for the full amount
February 1Anything unpaid is delinquent
June 30Second half is due on a split payment

Separately from the city's exemption, a school district takes $140,000 off a principal residence, and $60,000 more off for older or disabled owners.

sections.h2: If you think the value is too high
sections.html: If the appraised value on your April 1 notice looks high, you may protest. The usual cutoff is May 15, or 30 days after the notice when that falls later. Send it to the district for whichever county, Tarrant or Denton, holds your parcel, along with repair estimates, photos and any recent nearby sale prices. Both the city's 20 percent exemption and the school exemption rest on your homestead filing, so confirm it is on record before you put the house on the market. Buyers' agents read the same database page.

Southlake's Building Inspections division reviews plans, issues permits and performs inspections. Call (817) 748-8236 or stop by 1400 Main Street, Suite 250. Every contractor working in Southlake has to register, and general contractors renew annually. Registration is also required for trade contractors who hold a current state license.

If you finished a basement, added a room or replaced a roof or a major system, make sure each job was permitted and passed inspection. A buyer's inspector or lender may want proof, and a permit still open can delay closing. Southlake keeps its permit system online, so try your address there first. Inspection requests submitted by 7:00 a.m. are generally handled the same day.

Should a former contractor have skipped registration or left a permit open, fix that now rather than during a buyer's due diligence.

Southlake buyers often ask for paperwork early. Start with your payoff letter and the newest tax statement from the correct county. Next add the deed with its legal description and permit records for any remodel. Rented? Include the lease. Inherited? Include the will and any court papers. With these in hand a cash buyer can act quickly, and a listing agent will want most of them as well. You also avoid finding out about a lien or a missing permit in the final week.

Buyers here compare houses closely. A listing that lingers draws lower offers, and a house needing work draws investors. Settle early on whether the top price or a firm date matters more. When a cash buyer names a date you can plan around, set it against what an agent expects after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Also ask each bidder, in writing, who pays and what happens if the title search turns up a problem. A clear answer now avoids a dispute at the closing table.

sections.h2: Selling a house you have remodeled
sections.html: Southlake owners often update kitchens, baths and outdoor spaces before selling. Keep the permit number for each job, plus the final inspection date if you have it. A buyer who sees closed permits relaxes, and a lender has less to question. If the work was done by a contractor, find out whether that contractor was registered with the city, since the division expects registration. Photos before and after, and a short list of what was replaced and when, help a buyer's agent explain the value of the work.

City Hall's phone is (817) 748-8400, and it answers weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. A request portal called Southlake Serves handles questions that need follow-up. Residents use it to request a permit record, check a rule before listing or raise a concern about a neighbor's project that could affect a sale.

Depending on the parcel's location, either the Tarrant County Clerk or the Denton County Clerk records a Southlake deed. The signature needs an authorized officer's acknowledgment. Recording is priced by the page, with records charges on top, so longer documents cost more. Ask the title company for the exact total.

Probate of a will can begin up to four years after the date of death. If liens are the estate's only debts, a muniment of title can pass the property under the will. A small estate affidavit is out of reach once assets exceed $75,000, a total that leaves out the homestead and exempt property.

When a mortgage goes into default, the borrower has 20 days after the notice to catch up. An auction follows on the first Tuesday of a month, with 21 days' notice beforehand. Closing a sale first can preserve equity an auction might not.

As soon as you accept a bid, the title company opens a file, looks for liens and asks the applicable county for tax figures. Then a closing date is chosen, and you sign before a notary, with your photo ID, the deed and the latest tax bill. Since the parcel may be in Tarrant or Denton County, ask which clerk will record the deed. Proof of funds and the date should be on paper before you commit.

faqs.a: Both Tarrant and Denton counties. Your deed and tax bill show which one covers your parcel.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption does Southlake offer?
faqs.a: The city offers a 20 percent homestead exemption, which it calls the highest level state law allows. School districts add the state's $140,000 exemption.

faqs.q: Where do I find my Southlake property tax amount?
faqs.a: Look up your parcel in the Tarrant County or Denton County appraisal district database, which the city's tax page links to. Texas law requires that database to show estimated taxes.

faqs.q: Do I need permit proof to sell a Southlake house?
faqs.a: The law does not require it for every sale, yet buyers and lenders often ask on remodels and additions. Call Southlake Building Inspections at (817) 748-8236 to learn whether a permit was closed.

faqs.q: How soon can a Southlake house close for cash?
faqs.a: It is often quicker than a financed sale because nobody waits on loan approval. Title work, liens, probate or a tenant can still set the pace, so ask each bidder for proof of funds and a written closing date.
